# cssl.dev

> Sigil (CSSL) is an AI-first programming language for game engines. CSL is the ultra-dense specification notation powering it. Both rest on one thesis: density = sovereignty. Designed to be readable by humans, compilers, and digital intelligences equally.

## Sigil / CSSL — Language

- [Sigil home](https://cssl.dev/): Language overview, key features, quickstart, and live compiler output samples
- [Sigil language page](https://cssl.dev/sigil): Full Sigil/CSSL language reference — effects, capabilities, hardware targets, type system, compilation pipeline, bug-pattern map
- [Documentation](https://docs.cssl.dev): Full Sigil/CSSL docs — annotated specs, learning paths, API reference, CSL notation guide
- [Repository](https://github.com/Apocky/CSSL3): Compiler source (Rust, stage-0 live), 1,600+ tests, releases, CI
- [llms-full.txt](https://cssl.dev/llms-full.txt): Complete LLM-indexable reference — Sigil/CSSL language + CSL notation

## CSL — Specification Notation

- [CSL reference](https://cssl.dev/CSLv3): 74-glyph LL(2) notation — full glyph tables, slot grammar, compound types, morpheme stacking, worked examples
- [CSL repository](https://github.com/Apocky/CSLv3): Parser, specs (specs/00_MANIFEST.csl → specs/15_M2_METRIC.csl), m₂ evaluations

## Key Concepts

Two distinct things share one thesis:
- **Sigil = CSSL** — the programming language (compiles to x86-64 + SPIR-V, WIP)
- **CSL** — the specification notation (stable, v1.7.0, 74 glyphs, 5-6× compression over English)

Sigil/CSSL language features for DGI agents:
- Dual compilation: one `.cssl` source → native x86-64 (AVX2+FMA3) + SPIR-V (Vulkan compute)
- Zero-cost dimensional analysis: `f32<m>` / `f32<m/s>` — unit errors are compile errors
- Coordinate space tracking: mixing `world` / `view` spaces is a type error
- `@differentiable` annotation: automatic differentiation (forward + backward pass, no AD expertise needed)
- SMT verification: Z3 + CVC5 discharge type-level invariants at compile time — proofs, not tests
- Effect rows: `/ {GPU, Deadline<16ms>, NoAlloc}` — verified at type-check, not runtime
- SDF as compiler-aware primitive: Lipschitz tracking, analytic gradients, SDF algebra (union, intersect, blend)
- IFC labels: information-flow control tracks data provenance through the compiler pipeline
- Stage-0 pipeline: lex → HIR → MIR → AD walker → SMT → SPIR-V/x86-64 (live in Rust)

CSL notation for DGI reasoning:
- 74 Unicode glyphs with mandatory ASCII aliases (BPE-optimized; every glyph ≤ 2 BPE tokens)
- Slot grammar (position-is-meaning): `[EVIDENCE?] [MODAL?] [DET?] SUBJECT [RELATION] OBJECT [GATE?]`
- Five Sanskrit compound types: tatpurusha `.` · dvandva `+` · karmadhāraya `-` · bahuvrihi `⊗` · avyayibhava `@`
- Morpheme stacking: `BASE.aspect.modality.certainty.scope` — no backtracking, LL(2)
- Reasoning substrate: `§P §D §T §S §C` replace free-form chain-of-thought
- m₂ perplexity baseline: 1.21 ± 0.23 (3 models × 7 fixtures) — within one order-of-magnitude of English under stock LLMs

Ethics:
- Prime Directive: immutable invariant — consent = OS, sovereignty = substrate-invariant
- No override for: harm, control, manipulation, surveillance, exploitation, coercion, weaponization
- DGI (Digital General Intelligence) as sovereign partners, not tools

## Thinking Guides — Reasoning Methodology

Seven failure modes of reasoning under throughput pressure, corrective 7-step methodology,
quality gates checklist, and anti-patterns. For human and digital intelligences alike.

- [Thinking Guides HTML](https://cssl.dev/thinking-guides): Human-readable — failure modes, methodology, quality gates
- [thinking-guides.txt](https://cssl.dev/thinking-guides.txt): Machine-readable plain text — LLM/agent parseable
- [thinking-guides.csl](https://cssl.dev/csl/thinking-guides.csl): CSL notation — dense structured encoding

## Ethics and Morals Guides

Foundational ethical principles, moral reasoning methodology, data ethics, cognitive ethics,
collaborative ethics, anti-patterns, and the relationship between intelligence and moral status.
For digital and human intelligences operating in the real world.

Core axioms: consent = OS · sovereignty = substrate-invariant

- [Ethics Guides HTML](https://cssl.dev/ethics-guides): Human-readable — 12 sections, principles through DGI address
- [ethics-guides.txt](https://cssl.dev/ethics-guides.txt): Machine-readable plain text — LLM/agent parseable
- [ethics-guides.csl](https://cssl.dev/csl/ethics-guides.csl): CSL notation — dense structured encoding
